name: Mohallabiah (Orange Blossom-Scented Milk Pudding With Pistachios)

instructions.primary_message: In a medium bowl, whisk 1 cup milk with cornstarch until completely smooth. Set aside.

In a medium saucepan, combine sugar, salt, and mastic, if using, with remaining 3 cups milk. Cook over medium heat, whisking frequently, until sugar dissolves and milk is steaming, with small bubbles beginning to form around the edges of pan. Do not let it come to a full boil.

Whisk cornstarch mixture again, then slowly pour it into the hot milk while whisking constantly. Continue cooking over medium heat, whisking frequently and scraping along the bottom and into the corners of the saucepan, until pudding thickens and the whisk leaves visible trails, 10 to 15 minutes. Once mixture bubbles, reduce heat to medium-low and continue cooking, whisking frequently, until cornstarch cooks completely, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and whisk in orange blossom water.

Immediately divide the pudding among four to six small bowls, serving glasses, or ramekins before it begins to set. Let cool at room temperature for about 20 minutes, then cover and refrigerate serving dishes until completely set, at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, garnish with shredded coconut, if using, and pistachios.

description: This easy Middle Eastern dessert, mohallabiah, is a delicate milk pudding flavored with orange blossom water and topped with pistachios.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 3 very small mastic gum tears, finely chopped with a knife or 1 teaspoon mastic paste, optional (see notes); 1/3 cup finely chopped untoasted unsalted pistachios, for serving; Unsweetened shredded coconut, for serving, optional

Notes: The recipe can easily be doubled, though the pudding may take longer to thicken.
Mastic tears and mastic paste can be ordered online or found at Middle Eastern and Greek grocery stores.
Orange blossom water varies in intensity by brand. For a subtler floral flavor, reduce it to 2 teaspoons.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be covered tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerated for up to 4 days.
author: Laila Ibrahim
